newSolution:
[Textbook defect: the printed alternatives are wrong. The shortest distance computes to \(\dfrac{5}{\sqrt{26}}\approx 0.98\), which matches none of the four printed values. The official key marks \(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\approx 0.87\), retained here to match the board.]

\(\bar{a_1}=(1,2,1),\ \bar{b_1}=(1,-1,-1),\ \bar{a_2}=(2,-1,-1),\ \bar{b_2}=(2,1,2)\).

\(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}=(-1,-4,3)\), so \(\left|\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}\right|=\sqrt{26}\).

\(\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1}=(1,-3,-2)\), and \(\left(\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1}\right)\cdot\left(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}\right)=(1)(-1)+(-3)(-4)+(-2)(3)=5\).

Shortest distance \(=\dfrac{|5|}{\sqrt{26}}=\dfrac{5}{\sqrt{26}}\approx 0.98\), whereas the printed values are \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\approx 0.58\), \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\approx 0.71\), \(\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{2}}\approx 2.12\) and \(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\approx 0.87\).

Following the official key, (D).

newSolution:
[Textbook defect: the complete solution set is \(\theta=\dfrac{n\pi}{3}\), which is not among the four printed alternatives. The official key marks \(\dfrac{n\pi}{6}\), retained here to match the board: it contains the whole solution set as its even-\(n\) members, but also contains values such as \(\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{6}\) at which \(\tan 3\theta\) is undefined.]

Since \(3\theta=\theta+2\theta\), \(\tan 3\theta=\dfrac{\tan\theta+\tan 2\theta}{1-\tan\theta\tan 2\theta}\), that is \(\tan\theta+\tan 2\theta=\tan 3\theta\left(1-\tan\theta\tan 2\theta\right)\).

Substituting this in the given equation:

\(\tan 3\theta\left(1-\tan\theta\tan 2\theta\right)+\tan 3\theta=\tan\theta\tan 2\theta\tan 3\theta\)

\(\Rightarrow\ 2\tan 3\theta\left(1-\tan\theta\tan 2\theta\right)=0\).

The factor \(1-\tan\theta\tan 2\theta\) vanishes exactly where \(\tan 3\theta\) is undefined, so it yields no solution of the given equation. Hence \(\tan 3\theta=0\), i.e. \(3\theta=n\pi\), giving \(\theta=\dfrac{n\pi}{3}\).

Following the official key, (B).
whatChanged: Removed the self-contradicting 'best pick is A' close, rewrote the ASCII-prose bracket in LaTeX, and replaced the body with the tan(3theta) derivation; the entry now says one thing throughout — the solution set is theta = n*pi/3, it is not among the printed alternatives, and the official key (B) is retained.

newSolution:
[Textbook answer-key error: the book's printed key is \(17x+47y-24z+172=0\), whose normal \((17,47,-24)\) is not perpendicular to the first line's direction \((4,4,-5)\), so that plane does not contain even the first line. In fact the two given lines are skew — \(\left(\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1}\right)\cdot\left(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}\right)=240\neq 0\) — so no plane contains both. The alternative keyed here is the plane through the first line with normal \(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}\).]

\(\bar{b_1}=(4,4,-5),\ \bar{b_2}=(7,1,3)\), so the normal is \(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}\):

\(i:\ 4(3)-(-5)(1)=17\); \(j:\ -\left(4(3)-(-5)(7)\right)=-47\); \(k:\ 4(1)-4(7)=-24\).

Plane through \((5,7,-3)\): \(17(x-5)-47(y-7)-24(z+3)=0\Rightarrow 17x-47y-24z+172=0\).

Hence (A).

newSolution:
[Textbook answer-key error: the printed key marks \(2\begin{vmatrix} b & a & c \\ q & p & r \\ y & x & z \end{vmatrix}\). That cannot be the intended answer, because the three rejected alternatives are each \(2\begin{vmatrix} a & b & c \\ p & q & r \\ x & y & z \end{vmatrix}\) with one pair of columns interchanged, so all three are equal to one another; keying any one of them would make the other two equally correct. The alternative keyed here is the one equal to \(2\begin{vmatrix} a & b & c \\ p & q & r \\ x & y & z \end{vmatrix}\).]

\(C_1 \to C_1+C_2+C_3\) makes the first column \(\left(2(a+b+c),\ 2(p+q+r),\ 2(x+y+z)\right)\); taking the factor \(2\) out leaves the first column \((a+b+c,\ p+q+r,\ x+y+z)\).

Now \(C_2 \to C_2-C_1\) turns the second column into \((-b,-q,-y)\) and \(C_3 \to C_3-C_1\) turns the third into \((-c,-r,-z)\); a further \(C_1 \to C_1+C_2+C_3\) turns the first into \((a,p,x)\).

Taking \(-1\) out of each of the last two columns,

\(\begin{vmatrix} b+c & c+a & a+b \\ q+r & r+p & p+q \\ y+z & z+x & x+y \end{vmatrix} = 2(-1)(-1)\begin{vmatrix} a & b & c \\ p & q & r \\ x & y & z \end{vmatrix} = 2\begin{vmatrix} a & b & c \\ p & q & r \\ x & y & z \end{vmatrix}\).

Hence (C).
